title: Doppler Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits and Costs
summary: Doppler pricing includes free, starter, and professional plans with varying API request limits, user count limits, and monthly costs.
body_markdown:
## Automating Doppler Change Alerts With Activepieces


Activepieces won't lower your Doppler bill, but it can make sure someone hears about a changed secret or a failed sync before an outage does the telling.


It's optional, and a small team can skip it and lose nothing on price; its free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month if you do want it.


If you do want the alerts, Activepieces can receive webhooks from Doppler and turn them into messages in Slack, email or a ticket. It has an MIT-licensed core, 747 integrations counted in its public GitHub monorepo, and unlimited flows on every plan, free included.


That means your team learns the same day that a key was edited or a sync stopped, instead of finding out when an app starts failing.


Before building anything, check Doppler's documentation to see whether webhooks are available on your plan. That's a seat-and-plan question like the others in this article, and it's better answered before you build than after.


### Secret manager integration limitations


One boundary is worth stating plainly.


Activepieces' integration with external secret managers is an enterprise feature, listed in the enterprise governance set alongside SCIM, custom RBAC, SSO/SAML and audit logs, and "secret managers" appears by name in the feature list of the Ultimate plan on the Activepieces pricing page, which is priced through sales.


Point a self-hosted instance at your own secret manager and the connection credentials are absent from the Activepieces database, which is the table you can open and read.


So this workflow doesn't pull secrets out of Doppler into Activepieces. It only listens for Doppler's notifications. If you wanted Activepieces to read your secrets directly, that would sit on the Ultimate plan or the enterprise control tier, both quoted by sales.


The sketch below shows the whole shape. A Doppler project sends a webhook to an Activepieces flow, and the flow fans out to a Slack message, an email and a ticket, which costs 1 credit a run however many steps it has.


Read it as one signal in, three places it can land, and pick only the ones your team will actually watch.


### What the workflow does


Doppler sends a notice when something in a project changes. Activepieces catches it in a flow and passes it along.


You choose where it goes: a Slack channel for quick visibility, an email to whoever owns the project, a ticket if changes need a paper trail.


Most small teams need only one of the three. Start with the one people already check every day.


### When Doppler change alerts aren't worth building


If one or two people manage all your secrets and already sit in the Doppler dashboard, the alerts tell them what they just did. Skip it.


The same goes if your Doppler plan doesn't include webhooks, since you would be paying for a higher tier just to get a notification.


And a flow is one more thing that can break quietly. If nobody will own it, the upkeep cost from the previous section applies to the alert system too.
